The Great Mage's dungeon

Setting

Tka-Rik’s underground home links the two campaigns. He explains that Zak and Lu-a-Jalla have left to travel, listens to Kir’s account of Jigran and interprets the Magic Orb. The resulting clue directs Kir and Kel to Ingos. [1, 2, 3, 4]

Tka-Rik and the unknown allod

Meeting Great Magician Tka-Rik gives Kir his first direct contact with a free Joon magician. Tka-Rik explains that At-Zako and Lu-a-Jalla are travelling together and that he himself remains bound to Gipath. He has never heard of Jigran. Kir tells him about Firez, his enslaved family and his promise to return. Learning that more Joons need help renews Tka-Rik’s purpose. Since he cannot locate the hidden allod unaided, he sends Kir to find the Magic Orb that At-Zako once used. Finding the magician therefore begins another investigation rather than immediately opening the road home. [2, 3]

Babur’s rescue and the restored Orb

The stolen Orb stands on an island orc pedestal. Kir obtains the bridge gear from their gathering on Council Mountain to reach it. Once Babur is safe and has seen the damaged Orb, he provides the key to the observatory approach. The observatory book lets Estera prescribe washing the Orb in underground spring water. A landslide closes Kir’s former route to Tka-Rik, forcing him through the old tunnel. Before departure, Airy asks Kel to greet the Chosen if they meet him and says she still remembers him. Kel apologises for her earlier jealousy; both women recognise feelings Kir has yet to understand. The repaired Orb shows snow rather than Jigran. Tka-Rik interprets this as Ingos, agrees that Kel can go with Kir, and warns that greater freedom there does not prevent cruel government or make their search for powerful magic safe. [5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 4, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18]
